cues: The dry cell, inside every torch.
The zinc can itself is the anode, slowly eaten away.
A graphite rod in a mixture of manganese dioxide and carbon is the cathode, and a moist paste of ammonium chloride and zinc chloride is the electrolyte.
It gives about one and a half volts, and dies as the zinc is consumed and ammonia collects round the cathode.
text: The dry cell, inside every torch. The zinc can itself is the anode, slowly eaten away. A graphite rod in a mixture of manganese dioxide and carbon is the cathode, and a moist paste of ammonium chloride and zinc chloride is the electrolyte. It gives about one and a half volts, and dies as the zinc is consumed and ammonia collects round the cathode.
